questions.q: What does BRIM stand for?
questions.reason: BRIM is SAP's set of tools for billing subscriptions and usage: Billing and Revenue Innovation Management.

questions.q: Why is ABC Km (pay per kilometre) a good fit for BRIM?
options: The amount changes every month and comes from many small usage events
It has a fixed yearly premium
It is only sold to companies
questions.reason: Usage-based pricing with thousands of small events is exactly what BRIM's mediation, charging and invoicing are built for.

questions.q: Mette drives 820 km in May. Base fee DKK 199, DKK 0.45 per km. What is her bill?
questions.reason: 820 × 0.45 = 369, plus the 199 base fee = DKK 568.

questions.q: Which BRIM part collects raw events and removes duplicates and bad data?
questions.reason: Mediation is the front door: it collects, checks and cleans events before they are priced.

questions.q: Which BRIM part puts a price on each usage event?
questions.reason: Charging rates each event using the customer's price plan, for example 14 km × DKK 0.45 = DKK 6.30.

questions.q: Which BRIM part sells and manages the subscription itself?
questions.reason: SOM records what the customer bought, from when, and on which price plan.

questions.q: Which BRIM part collects priced items for the period and creates the invoice?
questions.reason: CI gathers billable items, runs billing and invoicing, and posts the invoice to FI-CA.

questions.q: What do FSCD and BRIM have in common?
questions.reason: FSCD is the insurance version of FI-CA, and BRIM's invoicing posts into FI-CA, so they share contract accounts, payments and dunning.

questions.q: Can Mette's home insurance (via FSCD) and ABC Km (via BRIM) be on the same contract account?
options: Yes, both post into the same FI-CA contract account
No, BRIM needs a separate company
Only if she pays in cash
questions.reason: Both feed FI-CA, so one contract account can hold both, with one combined bill or debit.

questions.q: After the BRIM invoice is posted in FI-CA, how are payments and dunning handled?
options: The same way as in Lessons 2 and 3
questions.reason: Once the open item is in FI-CA, payment runs, returns, dunning and the GL transfer work as before.

questions.q: What is a billable item?
options: One priced line waiting to be billed in CI
questions.reason: Each billable item knows the customer, contract, amount and purpose, and waits for the billing run.

questions.q: What is the difference between billing and invoicing in CI?
options: Billing collects and adds up items; invoicing makes the customer's bill and posts it
questions.reason: They are two separate runs: billing creates the billing document, invoicing creates the invoice and the FI-CA open item.

questions.q: What is a provider contract?
options: The FI-CA/CI record of what the customer subscribed to, linking partner, account and pricing
questions.reason: The provider contract tells billable items where to go: which business partner, contract account and price plan.

questions.q: A billable item has no matching contract. What happens?
options: It lands in an error status and must be fixed before billing
It is billed to a random customer
It is sent to the bank
questions.reason: Items that can't be assigned are held as errors, which is why the BA must define what happens to them.

questions.q: The same trip record is sent twice. Which part should stop Mette paying twice?
questions.reason: Removing duplicates is one of mediation's main jobs, before the event is priced.

questions.q: TeleNord sells ABC's phone insurance for DKK 49 a month with 15% commission. What is TeleNord's commission?
questions.reason: 15% of 49 = 7.35. BRIM's partner settlement tracks what each side owes.

questions.q: In a classic FSCD product, where is the premium usually calculated?
questions.reason: FSCD only bills the premium the policy system calculates. In BRIM, usage prices come from Charging.

questions.q: Which accounting standard covers insurance contracts?
questions.reason: Insurance contracts follow IFRS 17. RAR is mainly built for IFRS 15, so it is usually used only for non-insurance services.

questions.q: For an insurer, what might RAR be used for?
options: Non-insurance services such as a paid driving app or assistance service
questions.reason: Services sold alongside insurance may fall under IFRS 15. Always ask finance which standard applies to each part.

questions.q: Which product most likely needs BRIM?
options: Pay-per-day travel insurance sold inside a phone subscription
A pension with fixed monthly premium
questions.reason: Usage-based pricing plus a partner channel is a typical BRIM case; fixed premiums are fine with FSCD alone.

questions.q: A trip from 31.05 arrives on 03.06, after the May billing run. What should the BA define?
options: The rule for late events, for example bill it next month
Nothing, it is ignored by law
questions.reason: Late events need an agreed cut-off and correction rule; usually they go into the next bill.

questions.q: Which screen shows billable items that are waiting, billed or in error?
questions.reason: The billable item monitor is the BA's first stop when a usage charge is missing from a bill.

questions.q: Usage arrives after Mette cancelled ABC Km on 31.08. What should happen?
options: It is rejected or flagged and not billed
It is billed at double price
It is added to her home insurance
It is paid out to her
questions.reason: The provider contract has an end date, so usage after cancellation must not be billed. This belongs in your test cases.
